view: Retail sentiment is fearful (AAII bearish 48.4 vs 31.5 average, CNN F&G hit 20 on 11-06) but VIX at 17.62 shows no market-wide panic, and this week's 3.6x volume came with a gap down and new lows, not a reversal: so far it reads as forced distribution, not confirmed capitulation. Contrarian sentiment tilts mildly bullish over a quarter, but the 11-17 earnings binary and 5.9% daily ATR make the 2-week window wide and two-sided; tactical stance Wait until after the print.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 165.785. next_2_weeks: up = close > 174.07, down = close < 157.50, range between, measured at 2026-11-26 close. this_quarter: to 2026-12-31 last close; next_quarter: to 2027-03-31 last close; up = close > 182.36, down = close < 149.21, range between. up+range+down=100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=258). I cut range 45->33 because daily ATR is 5.9% and earnings fall inside the window, so a >5% move either way is more likely than usual; up +2, down +10 vs base.
Base 39/43/18 (n=253). Moved down +10 and range -7 for elevated volatility and an unresolved distribution week; up -3.
Base 50/31/19 (n=247). Kept up near base (-3); raised down +7 because the drawdown is not yet shown to be capitulation.

After weekly RSI <=36: 2w 46/23/31, 13w 69/0/31 (n=13, overlapping, autocorrelated). Weak evidence; it supports the contrarian up tilt but 31% down shows oversold-type readings fail often. Partly the same signal as momentum, counted once.
n=4 with 13w up 100%: too small to use; noted only, given ~zero weight. The weekly drop is -11.2%, and whether the 2w drop meets -15% is not in slice.

Week ending 2026-11-04: bullish 34.1 (avg 37.5), bearish 48.4 (avg 31.5), bearish up from 41.4 prior week. Elevated bearishness is a moderate contrarian positive, but the reading predates this week's -11.2% leg, so current retail mood is likely worse and unmeasured.

PARTIAL: 20 (Extreme Fear) on 2026-11-06; latest reported zone 'Fear' after a post-midterm rally, exact value not read. Fear has eased from extreme at market level while NVDA kept falling, so this is not a market-wide washout.
VIX 17.62: no index-level panic. NVDA's selloff is stock/sector-specific; a true capitulation low usually coincides with a volatility spike, absent here.
RSP +4.03% vs SPY -2.12% over 1m: money rotating out of mega-cap leaders into the broad market, consistent with distribution in names like NVDA rather than risk-off panic.

Monday volume 3.6x; Mon/Tue 462.7M and 429.3M shares vs 60d avg 130.1M (tv_chart_owner). Heavy volume on a gap down that stayed unfilled and new lows Thursday = distribution so far; capitulation would need a high-volume reversal/close back up, not yet seen.
Price 165.785 is below the week low so far 165.89: selling is still active intraday, no exhaustion signal.
Weekly RSI 33.3 (TV 33.13) on an open bar: not oversold (threshold 30); lowest since 2023 but the April 2025 low week printed 35.7, so this level alone does not mark a bottom.
Green bottom triangle 2026-11-10/11 is unconfirmed and price has since made a lower low; oscillator values not readable. Treat as unknown.

FAILED: no put/call, gamma or flow. I cannot tell whether earnings hedging is crowded (fuel for a squeeze) or complacent (room for further downside); this is the main reason confidence is 40, not higher.
-31.9% from ATH 243.37: bias audit - the ATH is an anchor that makes 165 feel 'cheap'; the base rates, not the distance from the high, should drive sizing.

key_levels.why: Fib 0.65 of owner's 10.81-243.37 range; nearest level below - a high-volume reversal here would be the first capitulation evidence. Check it is not chosen only because it is drawn on the chart (anchor).
Owner's swing label just below price; already being tested intraday.
Fib 0.618; a post-earnings flush into this zone on volume plus a VIX spike would look more like capitulation.
Bottom of the unfilled gap (179.92-185.22); reclaiming it would say the Monday distribution was absorbed.

what_would_change_my_mind: More bullish: a completed weekly bar (Friday 2026-11-13 close) with a long lower wick on volume >3x the 60d average, or a post-earnings close back above 179.92 (gap bottom).
More bullish: VIX spike with CNN F&G back into Extreme Fear and AAII bearish rising further while NVDA holds above 161.98 - a true washout profile.
More bearish: weekly close below 161.98 (fib 0.65) after the 2026-11-17 print with no volume reversal, or weekly RSI closing below 30 while VIX stays calm (orderly distribution continuing).
Options data becoming available showing heavy put demand into the print would raise my up probability (squeeze fuel); low put demand would raise down.
notes_for_chair: Earnings 2026-11-17 after close: BEFORE the print my 2-week view is near-symmetric (35/33/32) with range compressed by volatility; sentiment cannot forecast the print itself. AFTER the print, the reaction on volume tells us whether this week was capitulation (gap-and-go reversal) or distribution (continuation). Re-run my slice after 2026-11-18 close.

Bias audit for the owner: (1) ATH anchoring - -31.9% from 243.37 is not a valuation argument; (2) 'oversold = buy' - lessons log already caught this once; weekly RSI is 33.3 on an OPEN bar, not below 30; (3) urgency before earnings - there is no sentiment reason to act before 11-17; waiting avoids sizing into a binary whose positioning we cannot see (options data failed).

Stance (sentiment lane only): strategic Accumulate is not contradicted by sentiment (owner holds no recorded position; ladder levels are the owner's call); tactical Wait until post-earnings confirmation. No thesis break is signalled by my evidence (TB1-TB4 are for the narrative/fundamentals members).

Cross-domain: RSP +4.03% vs SPY -2.12% over 1m and VIX calm suggests a rotation out of mega-cap AI leaders - macro/relative-strength members should check whether this is sector-specific (SOX) rather than market-wide.
Equity Bottom/Top checklists are draft and unapproved; I have not scored against them.

Pre-mortem: it is three months later and this view was badly wrong - most likely because earnings triggered a squeeze from crowded bearish positioning that I could not see (options data failed), and the 4-sample 'drop >=15%' base rate turned out right.
